scenario: The Muro splits it early — a small group of the very best contests the wall
note: The most selective branch, drawn because the finish genuinely supports it and because the campaign has under-priced the shattering read before. The 600 m wall at over 10% arrives before the Pandera proper, so riders can reach the foot of the final climb already isolated, and the double-digit kilometres at 4.5-2.5 km to go are where a single rider can take minutes rather than seconds. References are the shattering-summit archetype (mountain 0.45-0.55, winner group 1): Pogacar's TdF 2026 stages 10, 14 and 3, Vingegaard's Vuelta 2025 stage 20 and Catalunya 2026 stage 6. The gap between this board and 'GC showdown' is how much of each contender's case rests on surviving in a group versus climbing with the very best when the road hits 15%.
